newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk shipyard signs deal to build 3 ships.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk shipyard signs deal to build 3 ships.

text.p: Poland's bankrupt Gdansk shipyard has signed a contract to build three ships, each worth $27.5 million, for German company Scholler Holdings Ltd, the yard's receiver said on Thursday.
The contract reawakens hope for reviving the historic shipyard, where the Solidarity movement that helped topple communism was born 17 years ago.

"On Wednesday, the shipyard signed a renegotiated contract to build three container ships...the project is to be financed by the owner of Polsat television, Zygmunt Solorz," receiver Andrzej Wiercinski told Reuters.
A firm conclusion of the deal still depends on the signing of a final agreement on financing, due next week.
An earlier contract with Scholler, to build five ships, was not implemented because the yard could not find financing under the proposed terms.
"The new contract puts off deadlines for completing construction of the ships and puts off payments of fines for failing to meet the deadlines," Wiercinski said.
Under the contract, the first ship is to be ready on April 20 next year and the last on September 30, 1998.

The contract will allow the rehiring of up to 2,500 workers by the yard, which has had to dismiss all but 370 employees out of its 7,000-strong workforce since June, 1996, when the company filed for bankruptcy with debts of 415 million zlotys.

The government is looking for an investor to buy the yard, whose book value amounts to $88 million. So far, 21 bids have been placed, including four serious ones, said Jacek Kwasniewski of BMF consultancy, which has been collecting the offers.
